title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: design custom AI agents with the AI development toolkit
summary: The briefing passes: its controls, capability default and consumption-based billing are supported by Microsoft documentation. It accurately distinguishes the sandbox-only designer from the production SDK and reports conflicting Microsoft statements about exports, permissions and operating costs.

claims.claim: A sandbox used by the toolkit can contain customer data copied from production.
claims.quote: Sandbox data: Can be used with customer data in sandbox environments (including sandbox copies of production data)

claims.claim: Learn advises against using the toolkit when compliance or security evaluation is the primary goal.
claims.quote: Don't use the AI development toolkit when: Compliance or security evaluation is the primary goal

claims.claim: Learn says agents cannot have more permissions than their creating user.
claims.quote: Permission inheritance: Agents can't have more permissions than their creating user

claims.claim: The permissions page describes task execution with the intersection of the scheduling user's and agent's permissions.
claims.quote: When a user schedules a task for an agent, the task is executed with permissions from the intersection of the user's permissions and the agent's permissions.

claims.claim: The transparency note instead describes intersection with the task approver or, without task approval, the agent configurator.
claims.quote: It then runs with the intersection of the permissions given to the agent with the permissions of the user that approved the task - or the user that configured the agent, if task approval wasn't required.

claims.claim: After user intervention, the task proceeds with the responding user's permissions, potentially a different user from the creator.
claims.quote: If the agent makes a user intervention request, the task continues proceeding with the permissions of the user that responded to that intervention request. This user might be different from the task creator.

claims.quote: InsertAllowed | Boolean | false, the insert action isn't allowed for the agent.

claims.claim: An agent profile's DeleteAllowed page-customisation property can disallow deletion.
claims.quote: DeleteAllowed | Boolean | false, the delete action isn't allowed for the agent.

claims.quote: it's recommended to build a custom profile for the agent in the same way as you would build a custom profile for a user.

claims.claim: UK, India and Australia environments are excluded from that initial model rollout.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing

claims.quote:
Billable agent capabilities

- Payables Agent
- Sales Order Agent

claims.claim: Credit consumption depends on agent design, interaction frequency and features used.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: Toolkit-specific Copilot Credit rates are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Central AI development toolkit custom agents Copilot credits billing rates price license quota; opened toolkit overview and Business Central consumption-billing page, and read Copilot Studio billing-rate search excerpts. No toolkit-specific rate was given.

claims.claim: The billing page publishes separate rates for Sales Order Agent, Payables Agent and Expense Agent.

claims.quote: Because your AI features are attached to your Azure OpenAI Service key, you're responsible for the operating costs of Azure OpenAI resources throughout development, testing and when your customers use the feature in production or sandbox environments.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost

claims.claim: Business Central supports pay-as-you-go agent billing.
claims.quote: Business Central supports two billing models: prepaid capacity and pay-as-you-go.

claims.claim: When both models are available, prepaid capacity is consumed first.
claims.quote: Both billing models can be used in the Business Central environment. When available, prepaid capacity is consumed first.

claims.claim: Without extra setup, Business Central environments consume credits from the tenant's default Power Platform environment.
claims.quote: Without any extra setup, Business Central environments automatically consume Copilot Credit capacity from the default Power Platform environment in your tenant.

claims.quote: It isn't possible to allocate capacity to specific Microsoft services or features.

claims.claim: The billing page says the AI capability is unavailable when quota is depleted until capacity is added.
claims.quote: When the quota is depleted, the AI capability is unavailable until more capacity is added.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The toolkit prerequisites and cited billing pages name no separate toolkit licence.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Central AI development toolkit custom agents Copilot credits billing rates price license quota; opened toolkit overview, creation page, transparency note and consumption-billing page. Prerequisites name permissions, sandbox and billing, not a separate toolkit licence.

claims.claim: Learn does not publish a feature-specific price for the toolkit.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Central AI development toolkit custom agents Copilot credits billing rates price license quota; opened Business Central consumption-billing page and toolkit overview. General credit pricing exists, but toolkit billing events remain a future update.

claims.claim: The Agent SDK for AL, unlike the sandbox-only designer, is available in production from version 28.1.
claims.quote: The AI development toolkit is available in sandbox environments only. The Agent SDK for AL is available in sandbox environments and, starting from version 28.1, also in production environments.

claims.claim: The Custom Agent capability must be enabled to design agents.
claims.quote: Before you can design agents in Business Central, ensure that you have the following prerequisites in place: Enable the Custom Agent capability in Business Central.

claims.claim: AGENT - DIAGNOSTICS grants access to execution-cost information in task log entries.
claims.quote: "AGENT - DIAGNOSTICS" gives you access to see the execution cost and the serialized page in the agent task log entries.

claims.claim: AGENT - DIAGNOSTICS also grants access to the serialised page in task log entries.
claims.quote: "AGENT - DIAGNOSTICS" gives you access to see the execution cost and the serialized page in the agent task log entries.

claims.claim: In Business Central, Search (Alt+Q) reaches Copilot & agent capabilities, where selecting a feature exposes Activate or Deactivate.
claims.quote: enter Copilot & agent capabilities, and then choose the related link. To turn on a feature, select it in the list, and then select Activate. To turn off a feature, select it in the list, and then select Deactivate.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no API that activates or deactivates the Custom Agent capability on the capabilities page.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Central Copilot agent capabilities activate deactivate API PowerShell capability configuration; capability table entity reference activation data movement API. Opened enable-ai and Copilot Capability codeunit reference; no administrative activation operation was documented.

claims.claim: Configuring capabilities requires SUPER permission or one of the listed Business Central administrator licences.
claims.quote: You need SUPER permission in your Business Central user account or one of the following Business Central licenses:

claims.claim: The design capability is listed under Production ready previews.
claims.quote: The design capability is listed under Production ready previews.

claims.claim: Business Central's Copilot & agent capabilities page contains the Allow data movement toggle for cross-geography processing.
claims.quote: enter Copilot & agent capabilities, and then choose the related link. Switch the Allow data movement toggle on or off as desired.

claims.claim: The toggle appears only when a capability might process data in another Azure geography.
claims.quote: The Allow data movement toggle appears when one or more copilot and agent capabilities might process data in a different Azure geography from the Business Central environment.

claims.claim: The cited documentation does not settle whether Allow data movement governs the Custom Agent capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Central Custom Agent data movement API. Opened enable-ai, ai-copilot-data-movement and toolkit transparency note. The control covers Microsoft-managed AI resources; the toolkit note instead describes the customer's Azure OpenAI key, leaving this case unclear.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no API for the Business Central Allow data movement toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Central Allow data movement Copilot agent capabilities API PowerShell Custom Agent geography; capability table entity reference activation data movement API. Opened enable-ai, data-movement page and Copilot Capability codeunit reference; no toggle-setting operation appeared.

claims.claim: The printed Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Prepaid capacity > Manage Capacity > environment > Copilot Credits route reaches credit allocation.
claims.quote: Select Manage Capacity from the Prepaid capacity card. In the allocation panel, select an environment and specify the number of Copilot Credits to allocate in the Copilot Credits textbox.

claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 writes the environment's credit allocation.
claims.quote:
$apiBaseUrl = "https://api.powerplatform.com"
$apiVersion = "2024-10-01"
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put `
    -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion"

claims.claim: The allocation request identifies the target with scope.environmentId.
claims.quote: scope = @{ environmentId = $environmentId }

claims.claim: The allocatedEntitlements array uses entitlementId MCSMessages for Copilot Credits.
The allocation quantity is set through allocatedEntitlements[].allocation.quantity.
claims.quote:
entitlementId    = "MCSMessages"
            allocation       = @{ quantity = 5000 }

claims.claim: The allocation tutorial requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent licensing-and-capacity role.
claims.quote: Sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.claim: Allocation applies to Business Central after linking its environment to the Power Platform environment, a task restricted to internal admins.
claims.quote: Link the Business Central environment to the Power Platform environment. Only internal admins can complete this task.

claims.claim: Some capability changes take effect immediately, while others require users to sign out and back in.
claims.quote: Some AI features take effect immediately, while others require users to sign out and sign in again.

claims.claim: Agent > Create > Create agent from scratch is the route to creating a blank agent.
claims.quote: select Agent > Create. In the Create agent wizard, choose whether to create a blank agent or use a template. To create a blank agent, choose Create agent from scratch

claims.claim: After agent identity details, the wizard offers Setup profile under Profile (role).
claims.quote: Under Profile (role), use the Setup profile option to select the profile that determines what UI elements the agent can see and interact with.

claims.claim: The wizard offers Manage permissions under Permissions.
claims.quote: Under Permissions, use Manage permissions to add the permissions that the agent should have.

claims.claim: AL Agent.UpdateAccessControl assigns an agent's permission sets.
claims.quote: The UpdateAccessControl method replaces any existing permission sets with the ones you provide

claims.claim: AL Agent.SetProfile assigns an agent's profile.
claims.quote:
// Assign a profile
    Agent.SetProfile(AgentUserSecurityID, 'ACCOUNTANT', SystemApplicationAppId);

claims.claim: Cross-application configuration is restricted, so those AL methods are not unrestricted administrator APIs for designer-created agents.
claims.quote: Creating instances, tasks, messages and any configuration changes targeting an agent defined in a different application is blocked with an error.

claims.claim: Business Central does not yet provide granular object-level permissions to limit Copilot configuration to particular administrators.
claims.quote: Business Central doesn't yet offer granular, object-level permissions so that only specific administrators can configure Copilot.

claims.claim: The allocation API tutorial requires an app registration configured for Power Platform API.
claims.quote: An app registration configured for Power Platform API.

claims.claim: TenantPool maps to Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.
claims.quote: The Draw from the available capacity in my tenant option in the admin center maps to the TenantPool enforcement rule

claims.claim: Enabling TenantPool allows consumption of unallocated tenant capacity after the environment allocation is exhausted.
claims.quote: when it's enabled, the environment continues to draw from unallocated tenant capacity after its own allocation is exhausted

claims.claim: The allocation tutorial describes disabling TenantPool as capping the environment at its allocation.
claims.quote: when it's disabled, the environment is capped at its allocation.

claims.claim: The capacity page separately lists Bill to my pay-as-you-go billing plan as an overage option.
claims.quote: Select Bill to my pay-as-you-go billing plan to let the environment continue usage through the selected billing plan.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Clearing both tenant-pool and pay-as-you-go overage sources limits the environment to its allocated prepaid credits.
claims.quote: If no overage source is enabled, the environment can consume only its allocated prepaid credits.

claims.claim: A published group rule governing tenant-pool draw blocks individual-environment overrides with TenantPoolLockedByPolicy.
claims.quote: If a published environment group rule governs Draw from the available capacity in my tenant, you can't override the setting for an individual environment. Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the TenantPoolLockedByPolicy error.

claims.claim: No toolkit-specific billing quota is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Central AI development toolkit custom agents Copilot credits billing rates price license quota; opened toolkit overview and Business Central consumption-billing page. They document environment capacity and pending toolkit billing events, not a toolkit-specific quota.

claims.claim: The roadmap recommends storing exported agent definitions in source control.
claims.quote: We recommend storing these files in a source control system like GitHub to track changes and maintain version history.

claims.claim: Exporting an agent definition supports backing up its configuration before changing instructions.
claims.quote: The purpose of this feature is to allow you to back up your agent configuration, share it with others, or move it between different sandbox environments.

claims.claim: The cited Assign permissions to users and groups page explains how to grant a permission set to a Business Central user.
claims.quote: You can assign permissions sets to users in two ways: From the User Card page, by selecting permission sets to assign to the user. From the Permission Set by User page, by selecting users that a permission set is assigned to.
